notes.cards-cashback-flat.dccFeePct: About 1% is charged on SGD transactions processed overseas or converted by DCC at Citi, DBS, UOB, OCBC, HSBC, Standard Chartered, CIMB, DCS, ICBC and Mari; not modelled per card.
notes.cards-cashback-flat.commonMccExclusions: Core SG card-reward MCC exclusions (almost every issuer, 2024-2026): 4829 money transfer, 4900 utilities, 5199, 5960/6300 insurance, 6010-6012 financial institutions, 6050/6051 quasi-cash & crypto, 6211 brokers, 6513 rentals, 6529/6530/6534/6540 stored value, 7349 cleaning/property management, 7511, 7523 parking, 7995 gambling, 8062 hospitals, 8211-8299 education, 8398 charity, 8651 political, 8661 religious, 9211-9223 courts/fines, 9311 tax, 9399/9402/9405 government. Frequent extras: 4784 tolls, 5047 medical supplies, 5993 tobacco, 7299/7399/8999 services, 8675/8699 associations, 9754 gambling.
notes.cards-cashback-flat.ewalletTopups: Every issuer reviewed excludes GrabPay/ShopeePay/YouTrip/EZ-Link/FlashPay top-ups (UOB Absolute pays 0.3% on Grab wallet top-ups). Bill-payment platforms (CardUp, ipaymy, SmoovPay, AXS, SAM, AMAZE) are excluded by HSBC, CIMB, DCS, DBS, Mari, GXS and Citi; AMEX True Cashback does not name CardUp/ipaymy (unverified).
notes.cards-cashback-flat.amexAcceptance: AMEX-network cards (AMEX True Cashback, UOB Absolute Cashback) are accepted at fewer SG merchants than Visa/Mastercard (hawkers, NETS-only merchants, some government billers); UOB AMEX cards do not support Apple Pay/Google Pay/Samsung Pay.
notes.cards-cashback-flat.grabCoinValue: GrabCoins are worth about S$1 per 500 coins (0.2 cents each) at standard redemption (MileLion, Aug 2026, secondary); GXS quotes its GrabCoin earn as % back.
notes.cards-cashback-flat.scEasyBillFeePct: SC EasyBill (IRAS tax, education, insurance, rent) charges a processing fee of up to 2.5% (raised from 1.9% around 1 Sep 2026), so paying these via EasyBill on a 1.5% card is net negative.
notes.cards-cashback-flat.trustFreedomModes: Trust Freedom is one card with four reward modes chosen per membership quarter (3 months from the approval month): Unlimited cashback, Bonus cashback, Stockback and Miles. The three cashback modes are mutually exclusive tiers of trust-freedom-unlimited-mode (this fragment); the Miles mode is trust-freedom-card-miles (cards-miles-general). Only one mode applies at a time; both entries share the card family 'Trust Freedom', so at most one is recommended as a new card.
notes.cards-cashback-tiered.gst: Annual fees quoted include 9% GST (e.g. S$180 + GST = S$196.20).
notes.cards-cashback-tiered.fxFees: Card FX fees: DBS/POSB, OCBC, HSBC 2.25% bank + ~1% network = 3.25%; UOB 3.25% all-in (UOB EVOL 0%); Citi up to 3.25%; SC 3.5%; BOC 3% (Visa/Mastercard) or 3.2% (UnionPay); CIMB 3%; Trust 0%. SGD transactions processed overseas / DCC typically incur 1%.
notes.cards-cashback-tiered.pointValues: SC 360 Rewards Point = S$0.003125 as cashback (3,200 points = S$10; used by the SC Smart card, encoded in cards-miles-specialised as sc-smart-card); POSB Daily$1 = S$1 (no expiry).
notes.cards-miles-general.milesValuation: Default 1.5 cents per KrisFlyer mile (MileLion acquisition benchmark, secondary; user-adjustable); ~1.7 cents as an optimistic bound, premium-cabin awards often more.
notes.cards-miles-general.cashOutFloors: Cash-out floors (official): OCBC 90N and DBS Vantage 1.0 cent/mile; SC 360 Rewards ~0.62 cent/mile; UOB UNI$ 0.5 cent/mile; AMEX Membership Rewards 0.6 cent/point (~1.2-1.32 cents/mile). HeyMax Max Miles pay for flights at 1.8 cents each.
notes.cards-miles-general.billPaymentPlatforms: Card bill-payment admin fees: CardUp list price 2.9% for Singapore cards; CardUp promo codes valid to 31 Dec 2026: income tax 2.25% recurring / 2.35% one-off / 2.30% 'Income Tax Bonus', rent 2.3% (official cardup.co/pricing, read 2026-09-28, recorded in research/brainstorm.md); ipaymy pricing page unavailable. billPaymentPlatformFeePct 2.6 sits between the promo and list prices. Bank facilities: Citi PayAll 2.6% (0.3% rebate with S$6,000 of payments, 1 Sep-31 Dec 2026), SC EasyBill reportedly 2.5% from Sep 2026 (secondary). HSBC, Trust (MCC 7399) and BOC cards earn nothing on these platforms, UOB cards earn nothing on ipaymy (CardUp earns), and Chocolate caps them at S$300 of bill payments per month.
notes.cards-miles-general.paymentFacilities: Bank payment facilities: UOB Payment Facility 1 mpd at a 1.6-1.8% promotional fee to 31 Oct 2026 (~1.6-1.8 cents/mile); OCBC VOYAGE Payment Facility 1 mpd at 1.9%; SC Visa Infinite income-tax facility 1.4 mpd at 1.9% (~1.36 cents/mile); DBS Points Purchase from 2 cents/mile.
notes.cards-miles-general.fxFees: FCY fees: 3.25% typical (UOB, OCBC, HSBC official; DBS, Citi, AMEX, Maybank secondary), Standard Chartered 3.5%, BOC 3.0%, Trust and Chocolate 0%. DCC / SGD processed overseas costs ~1% extra at UOB, OCBC, BOC, HSBC and SC and earns only local rates - pay in the foreign currency.
notes.cards-miles-general.conversionFees: Miles conversion fees: DBS, Citi, SC, Maybank and Trust S$27.25; UOB S$27 (waived with Reserve/VI Metal/VI/Privilege Banking); OCBC S$25; BOC S$30.56; HSBC, AMEX MR and KrisFlyer co-brands free.
notes.cards-miles-general.feeMiles: Miles credited on every payment of a NON-waivable annual fee are modelled as a 'fee-miles' tier (+miles/12 in any month the card is used): DBS Vantage 25k, DBS Insignia 100k, Citi Prestige 32k, Citi ULTIMA 150k, UOB VI Metal 25k, UOB Reserve 100k, UOB Privilege Banking 60k, OCBC VOYAGE 15k, SC Visa Infinite 20k, DCS Imperium 40k. Renewal miles on WAIVABLE fees (DBS Altitude, Citi PremierMiles, OCBC 90N, HSBC TravelOne) are not modelled, because the optimizer assumes the waiver and the miles are then withheld; SC Beyond's 80k renewal needs S$200k AUM (promo to 31 Dec 2026) and is not modelled. Cents per mile bought by paying the fee: DBS Altitude 1.96, Citi PremierMiles 1.96, Citi Prestige 2.04, SC Beyond 2.04 (promo to 31 Dec 2026), DBS Vantage 2.40, UOB VI Metal 2.62, SC Visa Infinite 3.0, OCBC VOYAGE 3.32, HSBC TravelOne 1.96 (KrisFlyer), OCBC 90N 1.96, DCS Imperium 3.24.
notes.cards-miles-specialised.milesPerPoint: Miles per point used for mpd rates: DBS Points 2 (5,000 pts = 10,000 miles); UOB UNI$ 2; Citi ThankYou 0.4 (25,000 = 10,000); HSBC Rewards 0.3333 to KrisFlyer (30,000 = 10,000) or 0.4 to Asia Miles/Flying Blue/BA/Qantas (25,000 = 10,000); OCBC$ 0.4; Maybank TREATS 0.4; SC 360 Rewards Tier 1 (Journey) 0.4, Tier 2 (Smart) 0.2899 (34,500 = 10,000, secondary); yuu Points 0.2778 (3.6 : 1).
notes.cards-miles-specialised.conversionFees: Points-to-miles fee per conversion: DBS S$27.25, UOB S$27, Citi S$27.25 (waived for ULTIMA / Instant Points Transfer), OCBC S$25 (secondary), Maybank S$27.25 (secondary), Standard Chartered S$27.25 (secondary); HSBC free until further notice; yuu and KrisFlyer UOB (direct miles) free. Minimum blocks: DBS 5,000 pts, UOB UNI$5,000, Citi/OCBC/Maybank/SC 25,000 pts.
notes.cards-miles-specialised.capDateBasis: Bonus caps reset by CALENDAR month on transaction date for DBS Woman's cards and DBS yuu; by calendar month on posting date for HSBC Revolution, UOB Preferred Visa, UOB Lady's, OCBC Rewards and Maybank XL; by STATEMENT month for Citi Rewards, UOB Visa Signature and the Standard Chartered cards.
notes.cards-miles-specialised.amaze: Instarem Amaze charges 1% (min S$0.50) on SGD transactions since 10 Mar 2025. Amaze transactions count as online for Citi Rewards (4 mpd) but earn nothing on DBS, UOB and KrisFlyer UOB cards (AMAZE* excluded).

notes.fx.convention: fxProducts.fxMarkupPct = the provider's disclosed fee or markup on top of the rate it converts at: the Visa/Mastercard network rate for bank debit cards and zero-fee cards, mid-market for Wise, or the provider's own rate (YouTrip, Revolut, amaze, iChange). It does NOT include the Visa/Mastercard network spread vs mid-market (~0.06-0.39%, see fx.networkSpreadVsMid), which also applies to every CreditCard.fxFeePct. This deliberately departs from the KDoc 'over mid-market' so FX products and card fxFeePct share one reference (the network rate); the network-rate products (Trust, GXS, Mari, DBS TravelLah!, UOB FX+) are therefore ~0.06-0.39% dearer vs mid than their 0 suggests, while Wise's 0.23 is all-in vs mid (on average about the same as the network spread). It also does not include undisclosed provider or bank conversion spreads (YouTrip, amaze Wallet, iChange, and loading DBS/OCBC/HSBC/Citi multi-currency wallets at the bank's rate). weekendMarkupPct is set only where weekend pricing is confirmed; unset = same as weekdays or not quantified. atmFeePct / freeAtmPerMonthSgd hold percentage ATM fees only; flat per-withdrawal fees (DBS S$7, Citi S$7, HSBC S$8, UOB S$5, iChange S$5) are in product notes. cashbackPct = cashback that FCY spend earns with no conditions attached (conditional programmes are in notes). The FxProduct schema has no validUntil: time-limited values are listed in fx.timeBound.
notes.fx.fcyFee.dbs: 3.25% on DBS/POSB credit and debit FCY purchases, refunds and reversals: Visa/Mastercard/AMEX 1% card-association fee + 2.25% DBS; UnionPay 0.6% + 2.65%. DBS AMEX was raised from 3% to 3.25% on 10 May 2026. Source: dbs.com.sg card-charges-and-fees-overseas-transaction-fees (verified 2026-09-28).
notes.fx.fcyFee.uob: 3.25% on UOB credit cards (secondary + sibling research); UOB debit cards 3.25% admin fee (official debit fee schedule, 18 Feb 2025) except UOB FX+ Debit 0%. UOB EVOL credit card 0% since 19 Jun 2025. Sources: uob.com.sg/debit/fees/debit-card-fees.pdf; milelion.com 29 Aug 2026 (secondary). As of 2026-09-28.
notes.fx.fcyFee.ocbc: 3.25% = 1% card association + 2.25% OCBC admin fee on credit cards (since 3 Dec 2019) and debit cards (since 6 Nov 2020) unless debited from the Global Savings Account. Sources: OCBC credit card fees & charges PDF (Jul 2024); OCBC debit card fee PDF (1 Oct 2025). Verified 2026-09-28.
notes.fx.fcyFee.citi: Up to 3.25% admin fee on FCY transactions on Citibank credit cards (Product Highlights accurate as at 19 Dec 2024). Citibank debit (Global Wallet) up to 2.5% incl. 1% Mastercard when not paid from a matching wallet currency. Verified 2026-09-28.
notes.fx.fcyFee.hsbc: 3.25% = 2.25% HSBC FCY transaction fee + up to 1% Visa/Mastercard charge on credit cards (2026 tariff). HSBC Everyday Global debit in non-EGA currencies (incl. RMB): 2.25% + up to 1% Visa. Verified 2026-09-28.
notes.fx.fcyFee.maybank: 3.25% on Maybank credit cards (secondary: milelion.com 29 Aug 2026; Maybank site unreachable).
notes.fx.fcyFee.americanExpress: 3.25% single conversion commission on Foreign Charges for AMEX-issued cards (Card Member Agreement, e.g. True Cashback card PDF). Verified 2026-09-28. DBS-issued AMEX: see fx.fcyFee.dbs.
notes.fx.fcyFee.standardChartered: 3.5% = 1% Visa/Mastercard + 2.5% Standard Chartered (highest among the majors). Source: sc.com/sg/pricing-guide (verified 2026-09-28).
notes.fx.fcyFee.bankOfChina: 3% on Bank of China credit cards (secondary: milelion.com 29 Aug 2026).
notes.fx.fcyFee.cimb: 3% = 1% Visa/Mastercard + 2% CIMB admin fee; CIMB Founders Card exempt (0%). Source: cimb.com.sg fees-charges/cards (verified 2026-09-28).
notes.fx.fcyFee.icbc: 2.5% administrative fee on non-SGD transactions on ICBC credit cards (2023 fee schedule + milelion.com Aug 2026, secondary).
notes.fx.fcyFee.zeroFee: 0% FCY fee (network rate only): Trust Bank (all cards, credit and debit), GXS (debit card, FlexiCard, GXS Credit Card), MariBank (credit and debit, from 1 Jan 2026), Chocolate Finance Visa debit, UOB EVOL, UOB FX+ Debit, DBS Chromo, DBS TravelLah! debit, CIMB Founders. Official product pages, 2026-09-28.
notes.fx.fcyFee.default: Assume 3.25% for an unknown Singapore bank credit card (derived from the issuer table).
notes.fx.networkComponent: Card-association component embedded in bank FCY fees: Visa/Mastercard/AMEX 1%; UnionPay 0.6% (DBS). Source: dbs.com.sg overseas transaction fees page (2026-09-28).
notes.fx.networkSpreadVsMid: Visa/Mastercard network rate vs mid-market: about 0.06-0.39%, varies daily (sample: USD 0.17%, GBP 0.29%, EUR 0.29%, AUD 0.06%, JPY 0.39%; milelion.com 29 Aug 2026, secondary). Zero-FCY-fee cards pay only this; it is excluded from fxMarkupPct and fxFeePct alike. Fetch network rates (or mid + typical spread) live rather than hard-coding.
notes.fx.weekendPricing: Revolut Standard: +1% on exchanges Fri 17:00 - Sun 18:00 New York time (Premium/Metal: none). Chocolate in-app SGD/USD FX guarantee fee 0.25% Mon 05:00 - Fri 10:59 SGT vs 0.50% Fri 11:00 - Mon 04:59 SGT. OCBC Global Savings Account online conversions are queued to the next working day on weekends. YouTrip and amaze Wallet weekend spreads are not stated (~1% generic widening reported for multi-currency wallets on weekends, holidays and volatile periods; secondary). Wise uses mid-market with no weekend markup. Visa/Mastercard-rate cards (Trust, GXS, Mari, Chocolate card spend, DBS TravelLah!, UOB FX+/EVOL) have no explicit weekend fee.
notes.fx.fairUsage: Revolut exchange fair-usage limits: Standard S$5,000 per month (1% fee above), Premium S$15,000 (0.5% above), Metal unlimited; currency, crypto and precious-metal exchanges count together; treat as a rolling month.
notes.fx.dccFee.dbs: DCC / SGD transactions processed overseas: DBS credit 1% card-association fee, no bank fee; DBS debit 2.8% (1% + 1.8%). Verified 2026-09-28.
notes.fx.dccFee.uob: SGD transactions processed overseas (incl. DCC): UOB credit 1% International Processing Fee (EVOL page, verified 2026-09-28); UOB debit incl. FX+ 2.8% (debit fee schedule 18 Feb 2025).
notes.fx.dccFee.ocbc: OCBC credit 1% on Visa/Mastercard SGD transactions processed overseas, incl. DCC and SGD online at overseas websites (fees PDF Jul 2024); OCBC debit 2.8% (debit fee PDF 1 Oct 2025).
notes.fx.dccFee.citi: Citibank credit 1% on SGD transactions processed outside Singapore (Product Highlights 19 Dec 2024); Citibank debit up to 2.5% incl. 1% Mastercard on DCC / different-currency transactions (2026-09-28).
notes.fx.dccFee.hsbc: HSBC credit Dynamic Currency Conversion fee 1% of the converted amount (2026 tariff, verified 2026-09-28).
notes.fx.dccFee.standardChartered: Standard Chartered 1% Visa/Mastercard charge on DCC and SGD transactions processed overseas (pricing guide, verified 2026-09-28).
notes.fx.dccFee.cimb: CIMB DCC fee 1%; Founders Card exempt from the network fee on SGD processed overseas per the fee-page wording (verified 2026-09-28).
notes.fx.dccFee.maribank: MariBank credit and debit: 1% Mastercard Currency Conversion Fee on SGD transactions processed overseas, incl. DCC and SGD at overseas websites (verified 2026-09-28).
notes.fx.dccFee.trustBank: Trust Bank: no fee on DCC; the DCC provider's rate still applies and DCC counts as Foreign Eligible Spend (credit card KFS, 4 Sep 2026).
notes.fx.dccFee.icbc: ICBC credit cards: DCC 1% (2023 fee schedule).
notes.fx.dccMerchantMarkup: The DCC provider's exchange-rate markup at merchants and ATMs is not disclosed by any bank and is not quantified. Always decline DCC and pay in local currency. DCC is excluded from DBS debit cashback, the DBS Live Fresh FX offset and UOB EVOL FX cashback; SGD-priced online purchases from foreign-registered merchants can also trigger the SGD-processed-overseas fee.
notes.fx.walletFallback: Multi-currency wallet fallback when the currency is not held: DBS My Account - FCY wallet insufficient => the ENTIRE transaction is taken from SGD at 3.25% (declined if SGD is insufficient). UOB FX+ with FX Debit ON => transaction DECLINED if the FCY balance is insufficient (FX Debit OFF => SGD at the Mastercard rate, 0% fee). OCBC Global Savings Account => falls back to SGD at 3.25%. HSBC Everyday Global => supported currency with insufficient balance is converted at HSBC's rate and billed in SGD (the product page says an admin fee may apply, amount not stated); unsupported currencies 2.25% + up to 1% Visa. Citibank Global Wallet => up to 2.5% per the terms (one FAQ line on the same page says no extra fees). Unsupported currencies (CNH on all bank cards; THB is only supported by DBS) always take the fallback path.
notes.fx.atmAllowances: Overseas ATM fees (operator fees may apply on top): YouTrip S$400 per calendar month free then 2%; Wise S$100 per month free then 1.75% on the excess; Revolut Standard S$350 or 5 withdrawals per rolling month then max(2%, S$1.49) (Premium S$700, Metal S$1,050); amaze 2% on every withdrawal (max S$1,000/day incl. fees); DBS debit S$7 per withdrawal (S$2 at select partner banks; free at Westpac group ATMs in Australia and DBS Hong Kong); OCBC GSA 3% (min S$5, max S$20) and free at OCBC ATMs overseas; UOB FX+ S$5 flat at non-UOB ATMs, first 4 per calendar year refunded, UOB ATMs in ASEAN free; Citibank non-Citi ATMs S$7 (Citibank ATMs free worldwide); HSBC network ATMs S$8 (HSBC ATMs overseas free; Premier EGA free everywhere); Trust debit and DBS TravelLah! no bank fee. Most e-wallet cards cannot withdraw in Singapore; GXS debit/FlexiCard and Chocolate cannot withdraw at any ATM.
notes.fx.walletLimits: YouTrip: max balance S$20,000 and top-ups of S$100,000 per rolling 365 days from the first top-up (official T&C). Revolut / Wise: S$20,000 balance and S$100,000 per year (secondary, MileLion). amaze: S$75,000 of transactions per rolling 12 months across NIUM-issued cards (official T&C 8 Sep 2026); wallet balance limit shown in app (S$15,000 per secondary). DBS TravelLah! wallet max S$5,000. Chocolate Visa: max S$1,000 per transaction and S$20,000 per day.
notes.fx.amazeRouting: Route only FCY spend through amaze Link (SGD spend costs 1%, min S$0.50). amaze Link costs up to 2.1% FX spread but the linked Mastercard sees an SGD online transaction with no bank FCY fee. DBS/POSB debit and DBS Woman's cards exclude 'AMAZE' transactions and UOB excludes AMAZE* (since 1 Oct 2024); DCS reportedly also excludes. Citi Rewards Mastercard earns 4 mpd (online bucket, travel MCCs excluded) on amaze Link, capped at 9,000 bonus points = S$1,000 per statement month: ~0.5-0.6 cents per mile at a ~2% spread vs the 0.4 mpd base. Wallet mode earns 0.5 InstaPoints per S$1 (0.25%-0.625% cashback or ~0.17 KrisFlyer mpd).
notes.fx.cardTopUps: Credit-card top-ups of wallets usually earn no card rewards (MCC 6540 etc.) and may carry fees: Revolut Singapore debit cards 0.30% (Visa) / 0.51% (Mastercard), international debit 2.08% (credit-card top-ups no longer listed on the Sep-2025 page); Wise card pay-in costs several %; amaze Apple Pay top-up 1.5% (min S$0.50). YouTrip's official T&C list top-ups as free but prohibit use primarily to earn card rewards. Prefer PayNow / bank-transfer funding.
notes.fx.wiseConversionFees: Wise SGD conversion fee for a S$1,000 conversion (price API, 2026-09-28; USD/EUR/JPY/THB re-queried, others from the same-day earlier pass): USD 0.23%, EUR 0.20%, GBP 0.24%, JPY 0.27%, AUD 0.19%, MYR 0.25%, THB 0.497%, KRW 0.47%, CNY 0.23%, HKD 0.23%, IDR 0.27%, VND 0.45%, PHP 0.40%, TWD 0.67%, INR 0.33%, NZD 0.22%, CHF 0.19%, CAD 0.19%. Volume discounts apply to large amounts.

notes.fx.trustFreedomBaselineMpd: 1.3 mpd = zero-FCY-fee miles baseline (Trust Freedom Credit Card Miles mode, per S$5 block, 0% FCY fee, uncapped; KFS 21 Sep 2026). Incremental cost of a fee-charging miles card on FCY = (fcyFee% + spread difference %) x 100 / (cardMpd - 1.3) cents per mile, using KrisFlyer-equivalent mpd (HSBC TravelOne 2.0, HSBC Visa Infinite ~1.67, HSBC Premier Mastercard 2.3 to KrisFlyer).
notes.fx.chocolate: Chocolate Finance Visa debit is a card (id chocolate-visa-debit, cards-miles-general fragment), not an fxProducts entry. notes.loans.creditCardApr: Card purchase APR: DBS, UOB, HSBC and CIMB 27.8%; OCBC 27.78%; Citi and Standard Chartered 27.9%; MariBank 27.99%; Trust personalised 18.9-29.9% for transactions from 1 Jul 2026. Once a statement is not paid in full, interest accrues daily from each transaction date, including new purchases (no grace period). Cash advances: 28.5% (DBS, UOB, HSBC), 28.92% (OCBC), 29.9% (Standard Chartered), 28% (CIMB), 27.9% (Citi) plus a fee of 8% (min S$15).
notes.loans.creditCardLatePenalties: Missed minimum: late fee S$100 at most banks (Trust S$200 when a loan instalment is billed; CIMB AWSM S$80; none at MariBank) plus a rate step-up: +3% p.a. at DBS and UOB until 3 on-time minimums; OCBC 30.78% and Citi 30.9% until not past due for the current and last 2 months; CIMB 29.9% until the next on-time minimum; MariBank 30.99%. OCBC and UOB apply payments to the highest-rate balance first.
notes.loans.creditCardMinPayment: Minimum payment: higher of 3% of the statement balance or S$50 at DBS, OCBC, UOB and CIMB (the market default); higher of 1% of principal plus interest/fees or S$50 at Citi, Standard Chartered and Trust; MariBank higher of S$30 or 3% of card spend plus 100% of loan instalments. HSBC's card formula is not in its tariff (S$50 or 1% for balance transfers). UOB's 3%/S$50 is from earlier research, not re-verified.
notes.loans.eirConvention: Singapore banks quote EIR as 12x the monthly IRR (nominal, with upfront fees at month 0 or billed in month 1). Merli's loan engine annualises as (1 + monthly IRR)^12 - 1, so its EIRs run slightly above advertisedEirPct (e.g. 5.20% nominal is 5.33% effective). Headline EIR bases differ by bank (amount, tenor, fees), so rank by recomputed cost, not headline EIR. Balance transfers: quotes assume equal monthly payments that clear the balance over the promo period, while banks' BT EIRs assume minimum payments and a final balloon, so quoted BT EIRs run above the advertised ones (the one-time fee itself is exact).
notes.loans.masUnsecuredCredit: MAS unsecured credit (Notice 635): minimum income S$20,000 for unsecured non-card credit (SC/PR) and S$30,000 for credit cards (S$15,000 above age 55). Per-bank aggregate unsecured limit: 2x monthly income for S$20,000-29,999 and 4x for S$30,000-119,999; above that banks set their own (OCBC/UOB 6x, Citi/CIMB/HSBC 8x, DBS up to 10x). Exempt: income S$120,000+, net financial assets over S$1m or net personal assets over S$2m. Catalog loans use maxIncomeMultiple 4 for this reason unless the bank states otherwise.
notes.loans.masBorrowingLimit: Industry borrowing limit: if interest-bearing unsecured debt across all banks exceeds 12x monthly income for 3 consecutive month-ends, no further credit is granted and existing facilities are suspended until the debt falls below the limit and the bank re-checks income and credit bureau. Credit limit management: once such debt exceeds 6x monthly income, no new limits may take total unsecured limits above 12x. 60+ days past due at any bank blocks new credit everywhere. Only interest-bearing balances count (cards rolled over past the due date, interest-accruing loans, late interest on 0% plans); secured, education, medical, business and qualifying renovation loans are excluded.
notes.loans.renovationLoanRules: Renovation loans up to the lower of 6 months' income or S$30,000, repaid within 5 years, are carved out of the MAS unsecured limits (Notice 635 para 7(1)(f)) and excluded from DCP.
notes.loans.dcpRules: Debt Consolidation Plan (ABS): SC/PR with annual income from S$20,000 (most banks S$30,000; Citi S$48,000 for non-customers; HSBC S$30,000-65,000 by relationship) to under S$120,000, net personal assets under S$2m, and interest-bearing unsecured debt across all banks above 12x monthly income. Consolidates all bank card and unsecured loan balances at one bank (not renovation, education, medical, business or joint debts); the first DCP adds a 5% buffer; other unsecured facilities are closed or suspended; a revolving card fixed at 1x monthly income is provided. Can be refinanced to another participating bank 3 months after the latest DCP approval (early termination fees apply and cannot be rolled in; no 5% buffer). 17 participating FIs incl. Trust Bank.
notes.loans.carLoanRules: MAS motor vehicle loans (agreements from 27 May 2016): max 70% of the lower of purchase price (incl. COE and taxes) or valuation if OMV is up to S$20,000, else 60%; max tenure 7 years. Used cars use an MAS-adjusted value and banks may use a nett price (e.g. UOB: price - S$200). Exempt: motorcycles, commercial vehicles (incl. private-hire cars under commercial schemes, e.g. GXS AutoLoan up to 100% over 10 years) and vehicles for disabled persons. Car instalments count toward TDSR. Flat-rate hire purchase refunds unearned interest by Rule of 78 on early settlement.
notes.loans.moneylenders: Licensed moneylenders: interest max 4% a month on the reducing principal, late interest max 4% a month on overdue amounts only, late fee max S$60 a month, upfront admin fee max 10% of principal, total charges capped at the principal. Aggregate unsecured caps: S$3,000 for SC/PR earning under S$20,000 (foreigners S$500 under S$10,000), 6x monthly income at S$20,000+. Unsecured loans disbursed from 15 Sep 2026 can be cancelled within 3 business days (repay the principal plus up to S$50, or up to 3.5% above S$5,000, of the approval fee). A last resort, outside the bank 12x regime.
notes.loans.governmentStudentLoanRate: HESL / government student loans: 3M compounded SORA + 1.5 pp (late: + 4.5 pp), reset 1 Apr and 1 Oct. 2.6% (late 5.6%) for 1 Apr-30 Sep 2026 (3M SORA 1.1226% on 27 Feb 2026); about 2.7% (late 5.7%) from 1 Oct 2026, derived from 3M SORA 1.186% on 1 Sep 2026 and not yet published. Legacy Tuition Fee / Study loans applied for before 1 Apr 2024 charge the average prime rate of DBS, OCBC and UOB, about 4.50% (4.25% / 5.00% / 4.25%; derived).
notes.loans.promoExpiries: LoanProduct has no validUntil, so these promotional rates stay in the catalog until the next refresh. Ending 30 Sep 2026: DBS used-car 2.68% and green-car 2.48% online promos, DBS Renovation 4.88% / Eco-aware 4.68% (usual 5.88% / 5.68%) and 3.38% home-loan-customer rate, Trust Instant Loan 1.00% (existing customers), and the OCBC Cash-on-Instalments, UOB PL, SC CashOne / Funds Transfer SG61, CIMB PL, DBS Reno S$188 and Citi Quick Cash GrabGifts cashbacks. Ending 31 Oct 2026: DBS PL 3% / BT 1% / Cashline cashbacks, Trust scratch card, UOB CashPlus 0% welcome offer. Ending 30 Nov 2026: OCBC EasiCredit cashback. Ending 31 Dec 2026: SC CashOne rate promotion. The HESL rate resets on 1 Oct 2026 (derived about 2.7% encoded).
notes.mortgages.provenance: Verified 2026-09-28 from research/mortgages.json: SORA from MAS domestic interest rates (value date 25 Sep 2026, published 28 Sep 2026); HDB rate from the CPF release of 22 Sep 2026; LTV/tenure, TDSR/MSR and stress-rate rules from MAS explainers (last updated 27 Mar 2024 / 29 Sep 2022); stamp duties from IRAS and MAS (3 Jul 2025); repricing and refinancing costs from OCBC, DBS and SC official pages; income ceilings and EC rules from secondary sources citing HDB.
notes.mortgages.sora: Compounded SORA (MAS, value date 25 Sep 2026): 1M 1.2505%, 3M 1.2302%, 6M 1.1559%, overnight 1.4974%. 3M SORA fell from 3.03% (Jan 2025) to 1.25% (Dec 2025), bottomed at ~1.03% (May 2026) and fixed at 1.186% on 1 Sep 2026. 6M SORA packages are not modelled.
notes.mortgages.hdbLoan: HDB concessionary loan 2.6% = CPF OA rate (2.5%) + 0.1%, confirmed for 1 Oct-31 Dec 2026 and reviewed quarterly. Loan amount assessed at a 3.0% floor with MSR 30%; up to 75% LTV (lower of price and valuation for resale; lower if the lease does not cover the youngest buyer to 95); 25% downpayment payable fully from CPF OA (may keep up to S$20,000 in OA); max 25 years or to age 65. At least one SC buyer; HFE letter needed; income ceilings from 24 Aug 2026 S$16,000 families / S$24,000 extended families (S$16,000 per nucleus) / S$8,000 singles 35+ (secondary sources); at most 2 HDB loans in a lifetime; 30-month wait-out for (ex-)private property owners. No lock-in or penalty; moving to a bank loan is one-way.
notes.mortgages.ltv: MAS LTV for individuals: 75% / 55% with no outstanding housing loan (min cash 5% / 10%), 45% / 25% with one (min cash 25%), 35% / 15% with two or more (min cash 25%); the lower tier applies if the tenure exceeds 30 years (25 for HDB flats) or the loan runs past age 65 (income-weighted average age for joint borrowers). Non-individuals 15%. Max tenure 30 years for HDB flats, 35 years for private property and ECs. LTV applies to the price net of any purchase- or loan-related discount, rebate or voucher (MAS).
notes.mortgages.tdsrMsr: TDSR 55% of gross monthly income (OTPs from 16 Dec 2021). MSR 30% applies to HDB flats and to ECs within MOP (new ECs from developers) and counts all property-loan instalments plus 20% of guaranteed ones. New residential loans are stress-tested at the higher of 4.0% and the package's highest 'thereafter' rate (non-residential 5.0%); HDB loans at 3.0%. Variable and rental income: at least a 30% haircut (12-month average). Financial assets are amortised over 48 months after haircuts (SGD deposits 0% if pledged >= 4 years else 70%; other assets 30% pledged / 70% unpledged). Owner-occupied refinancing is exempt from TDSR/MSR; investment-property refinancing above 55% needs a debt reduction plan (repay >= 3% of the balance within 3 years). Bridging loans repaid within 6 months are exempt.
notes.mortgages.stampDuty: BSD (from 15 Feb 2023), residential: 1% on the first S$180k, 2% next S$180k, 3% next S$640k, 4% next S$500k, 5% next S$1.5m, 6% above S$3m (non-residential tops out at 5% above S$1.5m); on the higher of price and market value. ABSD (from 27 Apr 2023): SC 0/20/30%, SPR 5/30/35% (1st/2nd/3rd+ property), foreigners 60%, entities and trustees 65%, developers 35% + 5%; joint buyers pay the highest applicable rate; married couples with an SC spouse buying a second home get ABSD refunded if the first is sold within 6 months. BSD/ABSD due within 14 days of signing. SSD on residential bought from 4 Jul 2025: 16/12/8/4% if sold within 1/2/3/4 years (bought 11 Mar 2017-3 Jul 2025: 12/8/4% within 3 years).
notes.mortgages.cpfHousingByLoanType: CPF OA use by loan type (CPF, 26 May 2026): new HDB flat with an HDB loan - the full price including the loan; resale HDB with an HDB loan - up to the Valuation Limit, then only after setting aside the BRS; bank loan (HDB or private) - up to the VL, then up to 120% of VL after setting aside the BRS. See tax.cpfHousing for lease-to-95 pro-rating and refunds.
notes.mortgages.ecAndHdbEligibility: EC income ceiling S$18,000 for EC sites whose land tender closed on/after 24 Aug 2026 (S$16,000 for earlier projects); ECs are bank-loan only with MSR 30% and TDSR 55% when bought from the developer; 5-year MOP; 30-month wait-out for (ex-)private owners. From 28 Jul 2026 (ex-)private owners buying a non-subsidised HDB resale flat without an HDB loan no longer wait 15 months (30 months still applies to subsidised flats, new ECs and HDB loans); they must sell the private property within 6 months. EHG income ceiling S$9,000. Income ceilings are from secondary sources citing HDB.
notes.mortgages.refinancingCosts: refinanceLegalFeeSgd S$2,200 + refinanceValuationFeeSgd S$300 = S$2,500, the midpoint of OCBC's official estimates (~S$2,000 for HDB, ~S$3,000 for private); brokers report ~S$1,800 legal for private and S$150-400 valuation (UOB S$150 + GST for condos; OCBC S$315 below S$1m / S$400 for S$1-2m). Discharge legal fees on redemption S$900-1,200 (SC). Redemption needs 2 months' notice (or interest in lieu); allow ~3 months. Bank subsidies are typically clawed back if redeemed within ~3 years.
notes.mortgages.refinancingRebates: Refinancing cash rebates are not modelled (legalSubsidySgd = 0 on every package): DBS S$2,000 (> S$500k) / S$2,500 (> S$1m) / S$2,800 (> S$1.5m) is broker-reported only; UOB's online rewards (S$2,000 cash + vouchers from S$300k HDB / S$450k private) close for applications on 30 Sep 2026 (LO by 7 Oct 2026); HSBC up to S$3,500 only for loans >= S$900k with HSBC Premier balances >= S$200k; OCBC's page shows a likely lapsed CNY cash reward; SBI subsidises refinancing legal, valuation and fire insurance (amounts not published). Check current offers before refinancing.
notes.mortgages.repricing: repricingFeeSgd S$800 = median of published same-bank repricing fees: OCBC S$500 (apply when <= 5 months of lock-in remain, >= S$100k outstanding, >= 5 years left), DBS S$800 (plus 1.5% if still locked in; repricing within the clawback period also claws back legal subsidies), SC S$1,000 (>= S$100k outstanding, >= 5 years left). Many packages allow a free switch after lock-in (freeConversionAfterYears), so repricing is often free in practice.
notes.mortgages.bankReferenceRates: Bank-set references: DBS FHR6 (6-month FD rate, S$1,000-9,999) 0.80% (secondary, 25 Sep 2026); SC FDR36 1.27% since 22 Aug 2025 (changeable on 30 days' notice); HLF HDB Home Rate 7.00% (12 May 2026) and Private Property Rate 6.15% (25 Sep 2025); DBS Prime 4.25%. Citi SORA packages have a 0.85% minimum effective rate; OCBC floors negative SORA at 0.
notes.mortgages.bridgingLoans: Bridging loans are not modelled (interest-only, up to 6 months): DBS at DBS Prime 4.25%, up to 20% of the new purchase price, no lock-in, min 1 month's interest; SBI S$30k-300k with an SBI home loan and proof of sale, no processing or prepayment fees. Exempt from TDSR if repaid within 6 months.
notes.mortgages.interestOffset: Interest-offset mortgages are not modelled: SC MortgageOne (private only; two-thirds of the linked deposit earns the loan rate, capped at the outstanding principal, the rest 0.25%; 1M/3M SORA + an unpublished margin (broker example 1.50%); min S$100k); HSBC SmartMortgage (offset on the lower of 70% of the loan and the deposit; hsbc-sora-smartmortgage is priced without it); Citi via its Cash Management Account. Compare the offset with prepaying the loan or high-yield deposits.
notes.mortgages.prepayment: Redemption/prepayment fee within lock-in is 1.5% (DBS and SC official; industry norm); DBS/POSB HDB packages charge 0%. Partial prepayment minimums: DBS/SC/HSBC/CIMB S$10,000 (multiples of S$1,000, 1 month's notice; CIMB at most once every 3 months), OCBC S$5,000. OCBC SORA: up to 50% of the loan penalty-free in the first 2 years; UOB promotion: first prepayment each year penalty-free up to 20% of the original loan; the UOB SORA promotion (official) and OCBC SORA package (broker-reported) halve the fee on sale; HSBC fixed-rate prepayments may add break costs.
notes.mortgages.brokerRates: Published and board rates are an upper bound; brokers quote negotiated rates for larger loans (indicative S$1m, Sep 2026): 2Y fixed from ~1.35-1.40% private / 1.40-1.45% HDB and 3M SORA + 0.20-0.25%. CIMB (broker 2Y fixed 1.55%; official min loan S$200k, income > S$24k private / S$36k HDB) and RHB publish no package rates and are not in the catalog.
notes.mortgages.modelling: Encoding conventions: each loan-size tier is a separate package (minLoanSgd/maxLoanSgd); ECs are included wherever private property is (completed packages for completed/resale ECs, BUC packages for new ECs); bank subsidies and cash rebates are not modelled. Board tables list years 1-3 only: unless the research states a 'thereafter' rate, the year-3 rate continues; 3Y/5Y fixed packages revert to the same bank's reversion on its other fixed packages; OCBC 1Y fixed and UOB board SORA tiers move to the bank's published +1.00% from year 4. Lock-ins the bank does not state are assumed equal to the fixed or promotional period (2 years for floating packages and for 1-year fixed packages, as SC and HSBC state for theirs). The DBS/POSB CPF-OA-pegged HDB loan is encoded as fixed steps (the CPF OA rate sits at its 2.5% legal floor). Where a bank offers the same spread on 1M and 3M SORA, 3M is used.
notes.savings-bonus.sdic-scope: SDIC insures SGD savings, current and fixed deposits and SRS monies up to S$100,000 in aggregate per depositor per Scheme member (all full banks and finance companies, incl. digital banks GXS/Trust/MariBank). DBS and POSB are one member. Foreign-currency deposits, structured deposits and investments are not covered. Source: https://www.sdic.org.sg/ (verified 2026-09-28).
notes.savings-bonus.sdic-cpf-schemes: CPF Investment Scheme and CPF Retirement Sum Scheme monies at a Scheme member are aggregated and insured separately up to S$100,000 per depositor; deposits held in trust/client accounts by non-bank depositors are insured up to S$100,000 per account.
notes.savings-bonus.typical-savings-rate: Typical prevailing base rate on major-bank savings accounts is 0.05% p.a. (DBS/POSB My Account, UOB One/Stash/Uniplus, OCBC 360, SC Bonus$aver); HSBC and Citi SGD accounts pay 0.01% (verified 2026-09-28).
notes.tax.provenance: Tax, CPF and SRS parameters last verified 2026-09-28 against IRAS, CPF Board, MOM, MOF (Budget 2026 annexes) and SDIC pages; confidence HIGH. MEDIUM items (notes only): CPF housing Valuation/Withdrawal Limit mechanics (secondary sources), UOB SRS cash rate (unpublished), OCBC CPFIA fee schedule (dated 2011). Key sources: iras.gov.sg individual-income-tax-rates, tax-reliefs, srs-contributions-and-tax-relief, tax-on-srs-withdrawals; cpf.gov.sg CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf, earning-attractive-interest; mom.gov.sg re-employment.
notes.tax.yearOfAssessment: Each year of assessment (YA) taxes the previous calendar year's income. Brackets (unchanged since YA2024) and the zero rebate are YA2026 values. YA2027 (income earned in 2026, when SRS contributions and CPF cash top-ups made in 2026 are relieved) is assumed identical until Budget 2027 (~Feb 2027). CPF contribution bands, wage ceilings, the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) are 2026 values, i.e. the income year being planned now.
notes.tax.brackets: Resident progressive rates on chargeable income: first S$20,000 0%; next S$10,000 2%; next S$10,000 3.5%; next S$40,000 7%; next S$40,000 11.5%; next S$40,000 15%; next S$40,000 18%; next S$40,000 19%; next S$40,000 19.5%; next S$40,000 20%; next S$180,000 22%; next S$500,000 23%; above S$1,000,000 24%. Cumulative tax: S$200 at 30k, S$550 at 40k, S$3,350 at 80k, S$7,950 at 120k, S$13,950 at 160k, S$21,150 at 200k, S$28,750 at 240k, S$36,550 at 280k, S$44,550 at 320k, S$84,150 at 500k, S$199,150 at 1M. Chargeable income = assessable income - min(total reliefs, S$80,000).
notes.tax.rebate: No Personal Income Tax Rebate for YA2026 (IRAS rebate page 11 Aug 2026; Budget 2026 has none). History: YA2025 60% capped at S$200, YA2024 50% capped at S$200 (computed after DTR/credits, before Parenthood Tax Rebate). YA2027 rebate unknown until Budget 2027: modelled as 0.
notes.tax.nonResident: Non-residents (not modelled by the engine): employment income taxed at the higher of a flat 15% or resident progressive rates, with no personal reliefs; director fees, rental, pension and other income at 24% (from YA2024; 22% before). Tax residency: SC/PR residing in Singapore, or a foreigner present/working >= 183 days in the prior calendar year (or 3 consecutive years, or straddling 2 years with >= 183 days).
notes.tax.earnedIncomeRelief: Earned Income Relief by age at 31 Dec of the income year: below 55 S$1,000; 55-59 S$6,000; 60 and above S$8,000 (disability variants S$4,000 / S$10,000 / S$12,000, not encoded); capped at earned income; automatic. Encoded as maxAge 54 / 59 / null against the profile's current age (approximation of the 31 Dec age test).
notes.tax.cpfRelief: Employee CPF Relief = compulsory employee contributions on OW (<= S$8,000/month) and AW (<= S$102,000 - OW subject to CPF); maximum S$20,400 at the 20% rate. Voluntary contributions above compulsory are not relieved (except via CPF Cash Top-up Relief). Self-employed: from YA2026 full relief on compulsory MediSave (uncapped); voluntary CPF relief = lowest of 37% x NTI, S$37,740 or the actual amount, each less compulsory relief. Self-employed MediSave rates (NTI > S$18,000, YA2026): 8% below 35, 9% 35-44, 10% 45-49, 10.5% 50+ (max S$7,104 / 7,992 / 8,880 / 9,324); none if NTI <= S$6,000.
notes.tax.cpfCashTopUpRelief: CPF Cash Top-up Relief: up to S$8,000 for yourself (own SA below 55 / RA 55+ / own MediSave) plus up to S$8,000 for family (parents, parents-in-law, grandparents incl. in-law; spouse or siblings only if their prior-year income <= S$8,000 or they have a disability); S$16,000 total. Relief-eligible amount limited to FRS - SA (below 55, incl. net CPFIS-SA) or FRS - RA (55+), and BHS - MA. Limits: YA2026 (top-ups in 2025) FRS S$213,000 / BHS S$75,500; YA2027 (top-ups in 2026) FRS S$220,400 / BHS S$79,000. RA accepts top-ups up to the ERS (S$440,800 in 2026) but relief only up to FRS. No relief for OA->SA/RA transfers, top-ups to non-family, MRSS-matched top-ups (from YA2026) or MMSS-matched MediSave top-ups made from 1 Jan 2026 (YA2027). Top-ups must be received by 31 Dec; a January top-up earns almost a year more interest than a December one.
notes.tax.srsRelief: SRS Relief = contributions made in the calendar year, claimed in the next YA: cap S$15,300 (SC/PR) or S$35,700 (foreigners, annual declaration to the SRS operator; relief only if tax resident; pro-rated recomputation if status changes to SC/PR during the year). Cash only, any time; employer contributions on your behalf are taxable to you and relieved. Contribute by 31 Dec - bank cut-offs are earlier: DBS 19:00 on the last working day of December via digibank; UOB 19:00 on 31 Dec (or preceding business day) via TMRW; OCBC requests 9am-9pm Mon-Sat, January contributions only from mid-January. No relief on amounts contributed and withdrawn in the same year; no refund of contributions when the relief cap makes the relief useless; no relief if the account is suspended at 31 Dec.
notes.tax.srsRetirementAge: SRS prescribed retirement age = statutory retirement age prevailing at the member's FIRST contribution, locked thereafter: 62 for first contributions before 1 Jul 2022, 63 for 1 Jul 2022 - 30 Jun 2026, 64 from 1 Jul 2026 (encoded, applies to new accounts). The move to 65 (~2030) is not yet legislated, so a token contribution now locks in 64. Existing accounts keep their earlier age.
notes.tax.srsWithdrawals: From the prescribed retirement age (also on medical grounds, or for foreigners withdrawing everything after a 10-year holding) only 50% of each withdrawal is taxable at resident progressive rates, in the YA after the withdrawal. Penalty-free withdrawals may be spread over 10 years from the first one; any remaining balance (except life annuities) is deemed withdrawn at the end and 50% taxed. With no other income S$40,000 a year (S$20,000 chargeable) is tax-free: up to S$400,000 over 10 years. Early withdrawal: 100% taxable plus a 5% penalty (bankruptcy: 100% taxable, no penalty). Terminal illness / death: taxable = 50% x (amount - [exemption - same-year medical/retirement withdrawals capped at S$40,000]), exemption S$400,000 if the 10-year window has not started, else S$40,000 x remaining years; no penalty. Withdrawing before contributing in the same year: the withdrawal is fully taxed with the penalty. SRS withdrawals count as income in dependant relief income tests (S$8,000).
notes.tax.srsWithholding: SRS withdrawals by foreigners AND PRs: 24% withholding on the taxable portion (withdrawals from 1 Jan 2023; 22% for 2016-2022), or 15% concessionary if calendar-year withdrawals <= S$200,000 and no other income that year (Form IR37B(1)). Not final: tax residents are assessed at resident progressive rates and non-residents at the higher of 15% or progressive rates, excess refunded; the 5% early-withdrawal penalty is separate and non-refundable. No withholding for Singapore Citizens.
notes.tax.srsAccounts: One SRS account at a time, with DBS, OCBC or UOB (age 18+, SC/PR/foreigner, not an undischarged bankrupt; no contributions after penalty-free withdrawals start). Uninvested SRS cash earns about 0.05% p.a. (stated by DBS and OCBC; UOB does not publish its rate). DBS: all SRS charges waived until further notice except S$2 per SSB application/redemption; SRS investments and dividends count toward DBS Multiplier 'Invest'. OCBC: S$2 per SSB application/redemption; share transfer-out S$0.35 CDP + S$10 per counter (+GST). UOB: charges waived except gold (S$5/certificate + S$72/kilobar p.a.), inter-bank transfers (S$3 per 1,000 units, max S$30/counter) and S$5 per failed/cancelled trade. SRS accounts are not encoded as deposit accounts because SRS money is capped, relief-linked and locked until retirement, not liquid cash.
notes.tax.otherReliefs: Other reliefs (entered by the user as otherReliefs; all within the S$80,000 cap): Qualifying Child Relief S$4,000 per child (disability S$7,500; unmarried child < 16 or full-time student, income <= S$8,000; shareable). Working Mother's Child Relief S$8,000 / S$10,000 / S$12,000 for the 1st / 2nd / 3rd+ SC child born or adopted from 1 Jan 2024, or born earlier but becoming SC from 1 Jan 2024 (other earlier children 15% / 20% / 25% of the mother's earned income; child order counts all children; QCR + WMCR <= S$50,000 per child, QCR allowed first; total WMCR <= 100% of earned income). Parent Relief S$9,000 per dependant living with you, S$5,500 if not but you spent >= S$2,000 supporting them (disability S$14,000 / S$10,000; dependant 55+ with income <= S$8,000; max 2 dependants). Spouse Relief S$2,000 (disability S$5,500; spouse income <= S$8,000). Grandparent Caregiver Relief S$3,000 (working mother, married/divorced/widowed, whose or whose husband's parent/grandparent living in Singapore cares for her SC child aged 12 and below and earned <= S$8,000 from trade/business/employment in the prior year; one claimant per caregiver, max S$3,000). NSman Self Relief S$1,500 without / S$3,000 with NS activities (key appointment holders S$3,500 / S$5,000); NSman Wife and Parent S$750 each. Life Insurance Relief only if CPF contributions < S$5,000: lower of (S$5,000 - CPF contributions) or 7% of the insured value / premiums paid. Sibling Relief (Disability) S$5,500 per sibling.
notes.tax.parenthoodTaxRebate: Parenthood Tax Rebate (offsets tax after the bracket table; not a relief, outside the S$80,000 cap; not modelled): S$5,000 / S$10,000 / S$20,000 for the 1st / 2nd / 3rd+ SC child, one-off per child, shareable with spouse, unused balance carried forward indefinitely.
notes.tax.lapsedReliefs: Course Fees Relief lapsed from YA2026 (MOF: no plans to reintroduce). Foreign Domestic Worker Levy Relief lapsed from YA2025.
notes.tax.donations: 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations to IPCs (a deduction, separate from the relief cap), extended to donations made 1 Jan 2027 - 31 Dec 2029 (Budget 2026).
notes.tax.cpfContributionRules: cpfContributionBands hold 2026 rates for SC and PR (3rd year onwards) employees with total wages > S$750/month. CPF's bands are '55 and below', 'above 55 to 60', 'above 60 to 65', 'above 65 to 70', 'above 70'; a worker moves to the next band from the month after the birthday that ends a band, so maxAge is 54 / 59 / 64 / 69 / null in completed years. Low wages: <= S$50 nil; S$50-500 employer share only; S$500-750 employee share phased in (0.6 x (TW - 500) at age <= 55). Total rounded to the nearest dollar, employee share rounded down. Max monthly on OW at age <= 55: S$2,960 total (employee S$1,600). Foreigners do not contribute. PR graduated rates not encoded: 1st year employee 5% / employer 4%, 2nd year 15% / 9% (age <= 55), full rates from the 3rd year or earlier on joint application.
notes.tax.cpfContributions2027: From 1 Jan 2027 (not yet in cpfContributionBands, which hold 2026 rates): above 55 to 60 employee 19% / employer 16.5% (35.5% total, max on OW S$2,840 / employee S$1,520); above 60 to 65 13% / 13% (26%, max S$2,080 / S$1,040); other bands unchanged; OW ceiling stays S$8,000. The increase goes to the RA up to the FRS, then OA. Employers get a one-year 0.25%-pt CPF Transition Offset in 2027 (no effect on employee take-home). Target 37% for 55-60 by ~2030.
notes.tax.maintenance: Update when the 2027 income year starts (1 Jan 2027): cpfContributionBands maxAge 59 -> employee 19 / employer 16.5 and maxAge 64 -> 13 / 13; cpfFullRetirementSumSgd -> 228,200 (limit for top-ups made in 2027); cpfBasicHealthcareSumSgd -> 2027 BHS once announced (normally December); after Budget 2027 (~Feb 2027) re-check the brackets and any YA2027/YA2028 rebate and set taxYearOfAssessment accordingly; re-check CPF interest rates quarterly (4% SMRA floor runs to 31 Dec 2027).
notes.tax.cpfAllocation: 2026 allocation (% of wage): 35 and below OA 23 / SA 6 / MA 8; above 35-45 OA 21 / SA 7 / MA 9; above 45-50 OA 19 / SA 8 / MA 10; above 50-55 OA 15 / SA 11.5 / MA 10.5; above 55-60 OA 12 / RA 11.5 / MA 10.5; above 60-65 OA 3.5 / RA 11 / MA 10.5; above 65-70 OA 1 / RA 5 / MA 10.5; above 70 OA 1 / RA 1 / MA 10.5. From 2027: 55-60 ratios OA 0.3382 / RA 0.3661 / MA 0.2957; 60-65 OA 0.1347 / RA 0.4615 / MA 0.4038.
notes.tax.cpfWageCeilings: OW ceiling S$8,000/month from 1 Jan 2026 (final step of 6,000 -> 6,300 -> 6,800 -> 7,400 -> 8,000; unchanged in the 2027 table). AW ceiling = S$102,000 - total OW subject to CPF in the year (S$6,000 with S$8,000 OW every month). CPF Annual Limit S$37,740 (37% x S$102,000) on all mandatory + voluntary contributions; MediSave cash top-ups (capped by BHS) and RSTU cash top-ups to SA/RA are outside it.
notes.tax.cpfInterest: 1 Oct - 31 Dec 2026: OA 2.5% (legislated minimum; pegged rate 0.32% for May-Jul 2026); SA, MA and RA 4% floor (pegged 12-month 10Y SGS + 1% = 3.06%), floor extended to 31 Dec 2027 (CPF, 22 Sep 2026). Extra interest (not in cpf*RatePct): below 55 +1% on the first S$60,000 of combined balances (OA counted up to S$20,000); 55+ +2% on the first S$30,000 and +1% on the next S$30,000 (counting order RA incl. CPF LIFE premium, OA up to S$20,000, SA, MA). OA extra interest is credited to SA (below 55) or RA (55+). Rates reviewed quarterly; interest computed monthly, credited annually.
notes.tax.cpfRetirementSums: Cohort turning 55 in 2026: BRS S$110,200 / FRS S$220,400 / ERS S$440,800 (ERS = 4 x BRS since 2025); 2027: S$114,100 / S$228,200 / S$456,400. cpfFullRetirementSumSgd = 2026 FRS: the cap on SA cash top-ups and OA->SA transfers below 55 and the relief limit for top-ups made in 2026. Estimated CPF LIFE payouts from 65 (2026 cohort, Standard Plan): BRS ~S$950, FRS ~S$1,780, ERS up to ~S$3,440 a month.
notes.tax.cpfBhs: Basic Healthcare Sum 2026 S$79,000 for members below 65 (fixed for life at 65); 2025 S$75,500; 2024 S$71,500; 2027 not announced as of 2026-09-28 (normally December). Voluntary MediSave cash top-ups capped at BHS - MA balance.
notes.tax.cpfAccounts: SA closed for members 55+ from Jan 2025 (SA moved to RA up to FRS, remainder to OA); at 55 an RA is created from SA then OA up to the cohort FRS. Below 55: cash top-ups (RSTU) and OA->SA transfers allowed up to current FRS - SA - net CPFIS-SA; 55+: RA top-ups (cash or OA transfer) up to the current ERS. Top-ups and transfers are irreversible; transfers get no tax relief and no MRSS grant.
notes.tax.cpfMatchingGrants: MRSS: S$1-for-S$1 grant up to S$2,000/yr (lifetime S$20,000) on cash RA/SA top-ups for Singapore Citizens aged 55+ (or below 55 with MSF-verified disability) with RA savings < S$110,200, average monthly income <= S$4,000, home AV <= S$21,000 and <= 1 property; automatic, grant credited by end-Feb; PayNow by 31 Dec or GIRO by 31 Oct. MMSS (Jan 2026 for 5 years): up to S$1,000/yr on MediSave cash top-ups for citizens aged 55-70 with MA < half of BHS and the same income/AV/property tests. Matched top-ups get no tax relief; the 100% grant beats relief at any marginal rate, so prefer it up to the grant cap.
notes.tax.cpfBudget2026TopUp: One-off Budget 2026 CPF Top-up (credited Dec 2026, automatic) for Singapore Citizens born 1976 or earlier owning <= 1 property: retirement savings as at 31 Dec 2025 < S$60,000 and AV <= S$21,000 -> S$1,500; S$60,000 to < S$110,200 and AV <= S$21,000 -> S$1,000; AV S$21,001-31,000 -> S$500 (either savings band). Do not top up to 'qualify'.
notes.tax.cpfLife: CPF LIFE payouts can start any time from 65 to one month before 80; each year of deferral raises payouts by up to 7% (up to 35% at 70). Plans: Standard (level), Escalating (starts lower, +2% a year), Basic (declines once balances fall below S$60,000). From 55: withdraw up to S$5,000 unconditionally plus savings above the FRS (or RA above the BRS with a property pledge lasting to 95). From 65 (cohorts turning 65 from 2023): up to 20% of RA as a lump sum.
notes.tax.cpfis: CPFIS-OA (age 18+, Self-Awareness Questionnaire, CPF Investment Account at DBS/OCBC/UOB): only OA above S$20,000 is investible; stocks <= 35% and gold <= 10% of investible savings. Agent bank fees: DBS S$2.73 per 1,000 units (max S$27.25) + S$2.18 per counter per quarter; UOB S$2 per 1,000 units (max S$20) + S$2 per counter per quarter (+GST); OCBC S$2.50 per 1,000 units (max S$25) + S$2 per counter per quarter (2011 schedule). Worth it only if expected return > 2.5% + fees. CPFIS-SA: only SA above S$40,000; hurdle 4% (5% within the first S$60,000). New CPF life-cycle investment scheme planned for H1 2028.
notes.tax.cpfHousing: OA can pay downpayment, instalments and stamp/legal fees. Usage above the Valuation Limit (lower of price and valuation) needs the BRS set aside and is capped at the Withdrawal Limit (120% of VL); WL reportedly does not apply to HDB-loan flats (secondary sources). Lease must have >= 20 years left; full usage only if it covers the youngest buyer to age 95, else pro-rated. Second property: set aside BRS (if the first lasts to 95) or FRS first. On sale, refund principal + accrued OA interest (2.5%). HDB concessionary loan rate 2.6% (OA + 0.1%, Q4 2026).
notes.tax.medisave2027: From 1 Jan 2027 MediSave 500/700 becomes MediSave Chronic and Prevent Care: S$700 a year (from S$500), S$1,000 for complex chronic conditions (from S$700).
notes.tax.retirementAge: Statutory minimum retirement age 64 and re-employment age 69 from 1 Jul 2026 (born on/after 1 Jul 1963: 64; 1 Jul 1960 - 30 Jun 1963: 63; 1 Jul 1958 - 30 Jun 1960: 62). The path to 65/70 by ~2030 is not yet legislated.
notes.tax.sdic: SDIC insures SGD savings, current and fixed deposits AND SRS cash up to S$100,000 in aggregate per depositor per member bank (DBS and POSB count as one); CPFIS and CPF Retirement Sum Scheme monies are aggregated and insured separately up to S$100,000. Foreign currency deposits, structured deposits and investments are not covered. Deposit plans should count SRS cash against the same bank's S$100,000.
notes.tax.approximations: Simplifications: earned income relief uses your current age instead of your age on 31 Dec of the income year, and the disability variants are left out; the CPF contribution band is picked from your current age and applied to the whole year (CPF switches bands from the month after the 55th/60th/65th/70th birthday, so a worker crossing a boundary this year pays the older band's lower rates for part of it); CPF contribution rates are the 2026 full rates (the 2027 senior-worker increases, graduated PR rates, low-wage rates and self-employed contributions are described in the notes only); the CPF OA, SA and MA interest rates used exclude extra interest; the Full Retirement Sum and Basic Healthcare Sum are the 2026 values that apply to top-ups made in 2026 (relief in YA2027), while the tax brackets and rebate are YA2026 values assumed unchanged for YA2027; the SRS statutory retirement age of 64 applies only to SRS accounts whose first contribution is made from 1 Jul 2026.

provenance.notes: Formerly the Trust Cashback card. One physical card whose reward mode is chosen per membership quarter (3 months from the approval month; switching is free and takes effect next quarter). The research lists the cashback modes as trust-freedom-unlimited-mode, trust-freedom-bonus-mode and trust-freedom-stockback-mode. They are encoded here as ONE card (keeping the default mode's id) with the modes as mutually exclusive tiers in group 'reward-mode', so the optimizer picks a single mode and counts the card once. The Miles mode (1.3 mpd) stays a separate entry, trust-freedom-card-miles in cards-miles-general, because it is a real alternative the cardholder chooses each quarter with a different reward type (miles vs cash), not a duplicate. Both entries share the card family 'Trust Freedom' (same issuer and base name), so the optimizer recommends at most one of them as a new card and does not suggest the other mode once one is held; a user who marks both as held could still see both used in one plan, although only one mode applies at a time. Merged 2026-09-28 with the duplicate entry trust-freedom-credit-card-cashback (cards-cashback-tiered), which encoded the Unlimited and Bonus modes of the same card without Stockback. Unlimited mode (default): 1.5% on Local Eligible Spend (SGD processed in Singapore), 0.5% on Foreign Eligible Spend (non-SGD, or SGD processed overseas incl. DCC); no minimum, no cap; credited on posting, rounded to 2dp per transaction. Stockback mode: 3% on local AND foreign eligible spend until 31 Dec 2026, then 2% local / 0.5% foreign from 1 Jan 2027; all stockback capped at S$500 per membership quarter (= S$16,666.67 spend at 3%; that the cap stays after 2026 is presumed); spend beyond the cap earns nothing. Paid as fractional shares of a pre-selected US stock/ETF once S$10 has accrued: valued here as cash at crediting, but it carries market and USD risk afterwards. The Stockback tier has minTransactions 1 only to keep it distinct from the Unlimited tier for the validator. Bonus Cashback mode: 1% local / 0.5% foreign on all eligible spend incl. the preferred category, plus 5% on ONE preferred category if eligible spend is at least S$500 in EACH month of the quarter (bonus cap S$30/quarter) or 15% at S$2,000 in each month (bonus cap S$250/quarter), credited the day after the quarter ends. Modelled as monthly tiers at total rates 6%/16% with the bonus caps converted to SPEND caps (S$600 / S$1,666.67 of category spend per quarter), beyond which category spend earns 1%. Bonus mode below S$500 (1%/0.5%) is omitted because Unlimited mode beats it. mortgages.name: HDB Concessionary Housing Loan
mortgages.notes: HDB flats only; at least one Singapore Citizen buyer and an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter needed. Household income ceiling from 24 Aug 2026: S$16,000 (families), S$24,000 (extended families), S$8,000 (singles 35+). Up to 75% of the price (or of the lower of price and valuation for resale); the 25% downpayment can be paid fully from CPF OA (you may keep up to S$20,000 in OA). Loan amount assessed at a 3.0% floor with MSR 30%. Max 25 years or to age 65. At most 2 HDB loans in a lifetime; 30-month wait-out for current or former private property owners. No lock-in or prepayment penalty. You can refinance to a bank later but never back to HDB.

mortgages.name: DBS/POSB 3-Year CPF-OA HDB Loan
mortgages.notes: HDB flats, new purchase or refinancing; Singapore Citizens and PRs. Pegged to the CPF OA rate (not SORA): always 0.82% (years 1-3), 0.40% (year 4) and 0.20% (year 5 on) below the HDB loan rate. 3-year commitment with zero early repayment fees; one free switch to another DBS/POSB package after 3 years. Up to 75% LTV over 25 years (age + tenure <= 65) or 55% over 30 years. Check the letter of offer for any legal-subsidy clawback. Free LPA certification until 31 Dec 2026.

provenance.notes: Official rates: CPF OA rate - 0.72% (years 1-3), - 0.30% (year 4), - 0.10% (year 5 on) = 1.78% / 2.20% / 2.40% at today's 2.50% OA rate. Modelling approximation: encoded as FIXED steps because the peg is the CPF OA rate (at its 2.5% legal floor), not SORA; the rate would rise only if the OA rate rises above 2.5%, and it cannot fall below these values.

Lock-in typically 2 years (1.5% penalty assumed, the industry standard); repaying during the fixed period may also incur break costs. HSBC terms: partial prepayment min S$10,000 (1 month's notice), full repayment 2 months' notice; package conversions carry an admin fee (waived only for HSBC Green Mortgage); default rate = contract rate + 3%. The S$3,500 refinancing incentive and 'as low as 1.49%' pricing need a loan >= S$900k and HSBC Premier balances >= S$200k (not included).

loans.name: DBS / POSB Personal Loan
loans.notes: Lowest published rate; the actual rate and fee are personalised at application. Tenors 6/12/24/36/48/60 months; loans of S$3,000 or less and non-SC/PR applicants: 6/12/24 months only. Foreigners need S$60,000 income; age 21-70. Interest allocated by Rule of 78; early termination fee S$250. Promo to 31 Oct 2026: 3% cashback on the approved amount, uncapped, for S$10,000+ over 36+ months applied online with code DBSPL (one per customer, clawed back if the loan is terminated).

provenance.notes: Modelling: cashback not included in quotes; the 1% fee is billed with the first instalment but quotes deduct it upfront; 4x monthly income is the MAS per-bank limit for S$30k-120k earners (2x for S$20k-30k, up to 10x at S$120k+).

Promo to 30 Sep 2026 (online, 48/60 months): 1% cashback for S$10,000-29,999, 2% for S$30,000+, capped at S$700, plus S$300 if new to Cash-on-Instalments in the last 36 months.

provenance.notes: Modelling: cashback not included; the S$30,000 income minimum is that of the underlying card or EasiCredit; 4x monthly income is the MAS per-bank limit.

Processing fee: higher of S$200 or 2%, deducted from the payout. Early partial/full repayment fee 3% of the amount repaid (min repayment S$1,000); late S$80. Up to 4x monthly income (6x at S$120k+).

Up to 2x monthly income (MAS limit for this band). OCBC points this income band here because EasiCredit no longer accepts it. Other terms as the OCBC ExtraCash Loan.

loans.name: DBS Further Study Assist
loans.notes: 4.38% p.a. on a monthly-rest (reducing balance) basis; 2.5% processing fee deducted at first disbursement (S$10,000 over 5 years = S$186/month). Up to 10x monthly (or combined) income, max S$160,000; 1-10 years. Guarantor aged 21-60, not bankrupt. Repay over up to 10 years, min S$100/month, no prepayment fee. Replaces the Tuition Fee, Study and OSP loans (closed 30 Jun 2026).

provenance.notes: Modelling: the derived 2.7% (from 1 Oct 2026) is used instead of the published 2.6% that ends 30 Sep 2026, so confidence is lowered from HIGH; the interest-free study period is not modelled.

provenance.notes: Modelling: fees unknown and not included; the tiered options (2.28% in year 1 then 6.28% for 6 years, EIR 9.04%; 2.99% then 6.99% for 7-8 years, EIR 10.35-10.41%) are not encoded.

fxProducts.name: YouTrip Multi-Currency Wallet + Mastercard
fxProducts.notes: Prepaid e-money wallet (MAS Major Payment Institution; not SDIC-insured); Singapore residents, no income requirement. No overseas payment fee and no currency-exchange fee; converts at YouTrip's own rate (marketed as wholesale). No explicit weekend fee, but the rate may widen outside market hours. 12 wallet currencies; card accepted in 150+ countries. Overseas ATM: first S$400 per calendar month free, then 2% (ATM operator fees may apply); no ATM withdrawals in Singapore. Max balance S$20,000; top-ups capped at S$100,000 per rolling 365 days from the first top-up. Top-ups are free, but credit-card funding usually earns no card rewards (MCC 6540 exclusions) and the T&C prohibit using YouTrip mainly to earn card rewards - top up by PayNow or bank transfer. No miles or cashback (merchant perks only). Card replacement S$10; S$10 refund fee on account closure.

provenance.notes: Official T&C and homepage read 2026-09-28. Approximation: YouTrip's own conversion spread vs mid-market is undisclosed and not included in fxMarkupPct (0 = official 0% FX/exchange fee); weekend widening unquantified, weekendMarkupPct left unset - confidence downgraded HIGH->MEDIUM. The 1.5% Visa-credit top-up fee reported by secondary sources is not in the official fee table. Daily ATM limit (~S$5,000; S$2,500 at Malaysian ATMs) is secondary only.

fxProducts.name: Revolut Standard (card + multi-currency account)

Exchanges outside FX market hours (Fri 17:00 - Sun 18:00 New York time) cost an extra 1%, including card payments that need a live conversion - hold the currency before the weekend. Overseas ATM: free up to S$350 or 5 withdrawals per rolling month (whichever comes first), then 2% (min S$1.49); no ATM withdrawals in Singapore. Top-up by Singapore bank transfer is free; Singapore debit cards 0.30% (Visa) / 0.51% (Mastercard), international consumer debit 2.08% (first card top-up free); credit-card top-ups are no longer listed. 5 free SGD transfers a month, then S$2.99 each. Card delivery S$4.99.

provenance.notes: Figures from archived official pages (live pages bot-blocked); a fee-page revision effective 25 Sep 2026 could not be read - re-verify in-app. Approximations: the S$5,000/month fair-usage limit (1% above), the 5-withdrawal ATM count limit and the S$1.49 minimum ATM fee are not modelled; Revolut's rolling month is treated as a calendar month. Confidence downgraded MEDIUM->LOW for these approximations (the 1% fee above S$5,000 a month is material for heavy spenders) and because the current fee page is unread.

fxProducts.name: Wise multi-currency account + Wise Visa debit card
fxProducts.notes: Multi-currency account with a Visa debit card (MAS Major Payment Institution; Singapore residents). Converts at the mid-market rate plus a variable fee from 0.19% (S$1,000 quotes on 2026-09-28: USD 0.23%, EUR 0.20%, GBP 0.24%, JPY 0.27%, AUD 0.19%, MYR 0.25%, HKD 0.23%, CNY 0.23%, THB 0.50%, KRW 0.47%, VND 0.45%, TWD 0.67%). Card auto-conversion uses the same pricing, with no weekend markup; spending a currency already held is free. Overseas ATM: free up to S$100 per month, then 1.75% of the amount above S$100; Wise cards cannot be used at Singapore ATMs. Card S$8.50 (digital card free; replacement S$4). Using the card to top up e-wallets costs 2%. Add money by bank transfer or PayNow - card pay-in is much more expensive.

provenance.notes: Official pricing pages and live price API read 2026-09-28. Approximation: fxMarkupPct uses the SGD->USD fee (0.23%) for every currency (actual 0.19%-0.67% by currency, see market note fx.wiseConversionFees); it is a markup over mid-market, whereas zero-fee Visa/Mastercard products are 0 over the network rate (~0.06-0.39% over mid) - confidence downgraded HIGH->MEDIUM. Balance/annual caps (S$20,000 / S$100,000) and 49 card currencies are secondary (MileLion Aug 2026). The effective date of the S$100 ATM allowance (reported 1 May 2026) is not on the official page.

fxProducts.name: Instarem amaze - Link mode (charges a linked Mastercard in SGD)
fxProducts.notes: Link up to 5 Mastercard credit or debit cards (age 18+, Singapore residents); switch between Link and Wallet mode anytime. In Link mode foreign-currency spend is charged to the linked card in SGD at amaze's rate: no bank FCY fee, but an FX spread of up to 2.1% (about 2% typical). Transactions are generally coded as ONLINE and keep the merchant MCC, so the linked card earns its own rewards (e.g. Citi Rewards Mastercard 4 mpd online bucket, S$1,000 per statement month, travel MCCs excluded). DBS/POSB debit and DBS Woman's cards ('AMAZE') and UOB cards (AMAZE*, since 1 Oct 2024) give no rewards on amaze transactions; DCS reportedly also excludes them. Domestic SGD spend in Link mode costs 1% (min S$0.50) - route only foreign-currency spend through amaze. No InstaPoints in Link mode. Transactions capped at S$75,000 per rolling 12 months across NIUM-issued cards. For 0%-markup spending use Wallet mode (listed separately); overseas ATM withdrawals cost 2%.

provenance.notes: Link spread (up to 2.1%) and 1% SGD Link fee (min S$0.50) confirmed on the official fees page; T&C updated 8 Sep 2026; DBS and UOB exclusions confirmed on their official T&Cs, DCS secondary. Research entry instarem-amaze is split: this entry is Link mode, Wallet mode is instarem-amaze-wallet. Approximation: fxMarkupPct uses the official upper bound 2.1% (typical ~2%, secondary). earnsFundingCardRewards is true in general, but DBS/POSB debit, DBS Woman's and all UOB linked cards earn nothing on amaze transactions (DCS reportedly too); FxProduct cannot restrict this per issuer, so the engine must check the funding card. Confidence downgraded HIGH->MEDIUM for these approximations. 'Best of Both' promo (8 Sep - 20 Oct 2026: 1,000-point bonuses for >= S$500 FCY spend by new users / >= S$1,000 by existing users, MCC 6540 excluded) not modelled.

fxProducts.name: Instarem amaze - Wallet mode (prefunded multi-currency wallet)
fxProducts.notes: Prefunded amaze Wallet (11 currencies, age 18+): no FX fee and 0% FX markup on foreign-currency spend (weekend spread not stated officially; ~1% reported by secondary sources); SGD spend from the wallet is free. Top up by PayNow or linked bank account (free); Apple Pay top-ups cost 1.5% (min S$0.50). Earns 0.5 InstaPoints per S$1 of eligible wallet spend, uncapped (FCY transactions under S$10, refunds, chargebacks and selected MCCs excluded; points expire 12 months after credit). Redeem 1,000 points = S$5 (0.25% of spend, unlimited), 2,000 points = S$25 at most once per calendar month (0.625% once 2,000 points - S$4,000 of wallet spend - accumulate within the 12-month expiry), or 3 points = 1 KrisFlyer mile (~0.17 mpd, plus a small admin fee). Overseas ATM (Mastercard/Maestro/Cirrus, overseas only): 2% of the amount, max S$1,000 per day including fees; operator fees may apply. Wallet balance limit as shown in the app (S$15,000 per secondary sources); S$75,000 of transactions per rolling 12 months across NIUM-issued cards.

provenance.notes: Wallet mode of research entry instarem-amaze. 0% markup, ATM fee and the Sep-2026 InstaPoints relaunch (earn in Wallet mode only; 1,000 pts = S$5; 2,000 pts = S$25 once a month; 3 pts = 1 KrisFlyer mile; 12-month expiry) are official. Approximations: cashbackPct 0.25 = the unlimited 1,000 pts = S$5 redemption, a floor (it needs S$2,000 of wallet spend within 12 months); the once-a-month S$25 redemption worth 0.625% for users with >= S$4,000 of wallet spend a year (on up to S$4,000 a month) is not modelled; the ~1% weekend spread (secondary) is not modelled - confidence downgraded HIGH->MEDIUM. Wallet balance cap is secondary only.

fxProducts.name: Trust Link card (debit mode)
fxProducts.notes: One Visa card with credit and debit modes; this is the debit mode, paying from the Trust savings account (credit mode is the Trust Link credit card). Foreign currency is converted by Visa (FCY->USD->SGD) with no Trust fee or markup; no Trust fee on DCC (the DCC provider's rate still applies), and SGD transactions processed overseas count as foreign. Overseas ATM (Visa ATMs; activate the overseas ATM function in the app): no Trust fee, Visa rate; ATM operator fees may apply. In Singapore, free at Trust and Standard Chartered ATMs. Cash withdrawn in credit mode is a cash advance (8% fee on amounts over S$5). No annual fee.

Randomised instant reward on each eligible transaction of S$10 or more (1.2x on Grab and Singtel Dash payments), unlimited; the expected value is not disclosed, so it is not included. fxProducts.name: DBS Visa Debit Card + My Account multi-currency wallets
fxProducts.notes: 0% FX fee when spending or withdrawing USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, NZD, HKD, CAD, THB, NOK or SEK from a funded DBS My Account wallet (DBS/POSB account holders); converting SGD into the wallet is done at DBS's rate, whose spread is not disclosed. (max balance S$5,000), topped up from a DBS/POSB account or the PayLah! wallet.
