fxProducts.notes: 0% FX fee when the OCBC debit card is the default card linked to the Global Savings Account (GSA), FCY debit is enabled and the GSA holds enough AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, NZD or USD (CNH not for card); converting SGD into the GSA is done at OCBC's rate, whose spread is not disclosed, and online conversions run only Mon 8am - Fri 11:59pm (weekend requests are processed the next working day at an estimated rate). Otherwise the card falls back to SGD at 3.25% (1% network + 2.25% OCBC). SGD transactions processed overseas (incl. DCC and SGD online at overseas sites): 2.8%. Overseas ATM FCY withdrawal from the GSA: 3% service fee (min S$5, max S$20 per withdrawal); free at OCBC ATMs overseas. No fall-below fee; interest only on AUD/NZD/USD above minimum balances. Card courier S$13.08; replacement S$20 + GST.

provenance.notes: All key numbers verified on official OCBC pages. Approximations: fxMarkupPct 0 covers spending a currency already held; OCBC's SGD->FCY conversion spread is undisclosed and not included; the S$5 minimum / S$20 maximum per withdrawal on the 3% ATM fee and the free OCBC-ATM withdrawals are not modelled - confidence downgraded HIGH->MEDIUM.

fxProducts.name: Citibank Global Wallet + Citibank Debit Mastercard
fxProducts.notes: 0% FX conversion or admin fee when spending or withdrawing from a Global Wallet currency account with enough balance; 15 currencies: SGD, AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, NZD, USD, AED, ZAR, SEK, NOK, DKK. Converting SGD into the wallet is done at Citibank's rate, whose spread is not disclosed. Other currency or too little balance: charged to the primary account with an admin fee of up to 2.5% (incl. 1% Mastercard) per the terms on the Global Wallet page (an FAQ line on the same page says insufficient-balance transactions carry no extra fees - assume up to 2.5%); the same up to 2.5% applies to DCC / SGD processed overseas. ATM: Citibank ATMs fee-free worldwide; non-Citi ATMs S$7 per withdrawal (charged in local currency) plus any acquirer fee. For Citibank Singapore account holders aged 16+ (individual or single-signatory joint). The Global Wallet page requires a minimum Total Relationship Balance of S$15,000 across Citibank accounts; the S$15 monthly fee below it is from the 2023 pricing guide (not re-verified).

provenance.notes: Verified on current official pages: 15 currencies, 0% from the wallet, up to 2.5% otherwise, S$7 non-Citi ATM fee, S$15,000 minimum total relationship balance (re-read 2026-09-28). Approximations: fxMarkupPct 0 covers spending a currency already held; Citibank's SGD->FCY conversion spread is undisclosed and not included; the S$7 flat ATM fee is not expressible as atmFeePct (left unset); the S$15 relationship-balance fee (amount from the 2023 guide) is not in monthlyFeeSgd - confidence downgraded HIGH->MEDIUM.

fxProducts.name: iChange multi-currency wallet + Mastercard
fxProducts.notes: Multi-currency wallet (MAS Major Payment Institution; Singapore residents) with ~50 currencies: you convert at a licensed money-changer partner's rate chosen in the app, and iChange says it adds no separate markup ('what you see is what you get') - the money changer's own spread still applies and varies. No card or ATM fee schedule is published; the ATM fee is reported as S$5 per withdrawal by secondary sources.

provenance.notes: UNVERIFIED: the official site discloses no card or ATM fees; figures are secondary. Approximations: fxMarkupPct 0 = no iChange markup on top of the chosen money changer's rate (that spread is unquantified); the S$5 ATM fee (secondary, flat) is not expressible as atmFeePct (left unset); annual fee unknown.

merchants.name: FairPrice (incl. Finest, Xtra, Shop)
merchants.notes: FairPrice Group supermarkets, Singapore's largest chain by a wide margin (commonly put at around half of supermarket sales). Singled out by Trust Link / NTUC Link (Linkpoints). OCBC Rewards also names Unity pharmacies, which count as in-store shopping, not groceries.

merchants.name: Sheng Siong
merchants.notes: Third-largest supermarket chain (about 70 stores), in store and online. Singled out by POSB Everyday (5%) and the BOC Sheng Siong card (6%). Share rounded down from about 20% of supermarket sales.

merchants.name: Cold Storage / Giant (incl. CS Fresh, Jasons Deli)
merchants.notes: Cold Storage (about 45 stores) and Giant supermarkets and hypermarkets; sold by DFI Retail Group to Macrovalue in 2025. yuu merchants on the DBS yuu card. Share rounded down from about 20% of supermarket sales.

merchants.name: 7-Eleven
merchants.notes: Convenience stores, counted with groceries. yuu merchant on the DBS yuu card. Small share: most grocery spend is at supermarkets.

merchants.name: Grab (rides)
merchants.notes: Grab transport in the Grab app (not GrabPay wallet top-ups). The clear market leader in ride-hailing (commonly put at 60% or more). Singled out by the GXS Credit Card, UOB One, AMEX KrisFlyer (first S$200 a month) and others. GrabFood and GrabMart are listed separately.

merchants.name: Gojek
merchants.notes: Second-largest ride-hailing app (rides only in Singapore). yuu merchant on the DBS yuu card. Conservative estimate; TADA, Ryde and CDG Zig/street taxis make up most of the rest.

merchants.name: GrabFood & GrabMart
merchants.notes: Grab food and grocery delivery in the Grab app. The largest delivery platform; Deliveroo left Singapore on 4 Mar 2026, leaving Grab and foodpanda as the two main apps. Singled out by the GXS Credit Card, UOB One, AMEX KrisFlyer and POSB Everyday (with foodpanda).

merchants.name: foodpanda (incl. pandamart)
merchants.notes: Second-largest delivery platform. yuu merchant on the DBS yuu card; POSB Everyday pays its delivery bonus only at foodpanda and GrabFood. Conservative estimate; own-app orders (McDelivery, Domino's, Pizza Hut) make up most of the rest.

merchants.name: SimplyGo (MRT & bus fares)
merchants.notes: All MRT and bus fares paid by tapping a bank card or phone go through SimplyGo (account-based ticketing), so it covers essentially the whole category. Singled out by DBS yuu, POSB Everyday, UOB One, SC Smart, OCBC Frank and others. EZ-Link and SimplyGo top-ups are a different thing and rarely earn.

merchants.name: Shopee
merchants.notes: Singapore's largest online marketplace (incl. Shopee Supermarket; not ShopeePay top-ups). Singled out by UOB One, POSB Everyday, OCBC Rewards (15X promo) and Mari. Online shopping also covers brand sites, Qoo10, Zalora and the like, so the share is well below Shopee's share of marketplace sales.

merchants.name: Lazada (incl. RedMart)
merchants.notes: Second-largest marketplace; RedMart groceries are part of Lazada. Singled out by POSB Everyday and OCBC Rewards (15X promo).

merchants.name: Amazon (Amazon.sg and Amazon.com)
merchants.notes: Amazon.sg charges in SGD; Amazon.com and other Amazon stores usually charge in a foreign currency. Singled out by POSB Everyday (Amazon.sg) and OCBC Rewards.

merchants.name: TikTok Shop
merchants.notes: Singled out by POSB Everyday and OCBC Rewards (15X promo). Smaller than Shopee and Lazada in Singapore.

merchants.name: Taobao
merchants.notes: Singled out by POSB Everyday and OCBC Rewards (15X promo). Depending on checkout it may be charged in SGD or in a foreign currency, so both online categories are listed; the share is kept low for both.

merchants.name: Watsons
merchants.notes: Health and beauty stores. Singled out by OCBC 365 (3%) and OCBC Rewards (15X promo). Watsons orders on Lazada, Shopee or Amazon count as those marketplaces, not Watsons. Online orders at watsons.com.sg are not covered by this default.

merchants.name: Guardian
merchants.notes: Health and beauty stores. yuu merchant on the DBS yuu card; named by OCBC Rewards.

merchants.name: POPULAR bookstores
merchants.notes: Books and stationery, in store and online. Singled out by POSB Everyday (5% with S$800 monthly spend).

merchants.name: Pet Lovers Centre
merchants.notes: Pet supplies. Singled out by POSB Everyday (3%). Only relevant to pet owners; raise the share if you shop there.

merchants.name: Shell
merchants.notes: One of the two largest petrol networks. Singled out by UOB One (Tier 3) and HSBC Live+ (with Caltex); excluded by most UOB miles cards. Petrol brand choice is very personal, so set your own share if you mostly fill up in one place.

merchants.name: Esso
merchants.notes: 58 stations, one of the two largest networks. Earns the UOB Visa Signature petrol bonus (which excludes SPC and Shell). The Maybank World Mastercard petrol bonus does not count payments made through apps such as Kris+ at Esso.

merchants.name: SPC
merchants.notes: Third-largest petrol network. Singled out by POSB Everyday (6% on top of SPC discounts) and earns on UOB PRVI Miles AMEX; excluded by most other UOB cards.

merchants.name: Caltex
merchants.notes: A smaller petrol network. Singled out by HSBC Live+ (with Shell) and earns the UOB Visa Signature petrol bonus. The Maybank World Mastercard petrol bonus does not count payments made through the CaltexGo app.

merchants.name: Sinopec
merchants.notes: A handful of stations. Earns the UOB Visa Signature petrol bonus (which excludes SPC and Shell).

merchants.name: Charge+ (EV charging)
merchants.notes: Electric-vehicle charging network, counted with petrol as car energy. yuu merchant on the DBS yuu card (Visa only), an OCBC Frank green merchant, and the stand-in for EV charging in the SC Smart bonus (until 31 Dec 2026). Most drivers still use petrol; raise the share if you drive an EV and charge at Charge+.

merchants.name: Singapore Airlines, Scoot & Pelago
merchants.notes: Bookings paid directly to Singapore Airlines or Scoot, plus Pelago experiences (KrisShop and Kris+ purchases also qualify but sit in other categories). Singled out by the KrisFlyer UOB card (3 mpd) and the AMEX KrisFlyer cards (2 mpd); AMEX Platinum Charge counts only Singapore Airlines and Scoot. Estimate: SIA and Scoot carry roughly half of residents' flights, and flights are a bit over half of travel-booking spend (the rest is hotels and other airlines).

merchants.name: Agoda
merchants.notes: A leading hotel-booking site in Asia. Bonus-miles offers (Citi PremierMiles, UOB PRVI Miles, OCBC 90°N) need prepaid bookings through the card's own Agoda link. Bookings charged in a foreign currency count as online foreign-currency spend instead.

merchants.name: Expedia
merchants.notes: Bonus-miles offer on UOB PRVI Miles (bookings through the card's own Expedia link). Smaller than Agoda for Singapore travellers.

merchants.name: Kaligo
merchants.notes: Hotel-booking site built around bonus miles (Citi PremierMiles offer via its own Kaligo link). Few people book there by default; raise the share if you do.

merchants.name: Streaming (Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, YouTube Premium, Prime Video...)
merchants.notes: Video and music streaming subscriptions. SC Smart lists Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, YouTube, Amazon Prime Video, HBO GO, iQIYI and Viu; UOB EVOL lists Netflix, Spotify and Disney+; OCBC 365 counts streaming generally. The rest of entertainment spend is cinema, concerts and events.

merchants.name: Fast-food & coffee chains (McDonald's, KFC, Burger King, Starbucks, Toast Box, Ya Kun...)
merchants.notes: SC Smart bonus merchants: Burger King, Domino's, KFC, McDonald's, Pizza Hut, Starbucks, Subway, The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf, Toast Box and Ya Kun Kaya Toast, in store or through their own apps (orders placed through GrabFood or foodpanda count as those apps). Includes McDonald's, which is also listed on its own.

merchants.name: McDonald's (incl. McDelivery)
merchants.notes: Singled out by UOB One (with Grab, Shopee and SimplyGo). McDelivery ordered in McDonald's own app counts; orders placed through GrabFood or foodpanda count as those apps.

merchants.name: CHAGEE (app orders)
merchants.notes: Tea drinks ordered in the CHAGEE app. yuu merchant on the DBS yuu card. Raise the share if you are a regular.

merchants.name: SP Group utilities bill
merchants.notes: The SP Services bill (electricity on the regulated tariff, water, gas and refuse). Singled out by UOB One (1%). Most other cards exclude utilities. Estimate: a typical household's SP bill is somewhat less than half of its utilities and telco bills; electricity bought from an Open Electric Market retailer is billed by that retailer instead.

merchants.name: Mobile & broadband bills (Singtel, StarHub, M1, MyRepublic, Circles.Life...)
merchants.notes: Telco bills charged to the card. UOB EVOL (Singtel, StarHub, M1, Gomo, MyRepublic, Giga, CirclesLife) and Maybank Family & Friends pay a bonus on telco but not on utilities; OCBC 365 needs telco and electricity bills set up as recurring card payments. Includes Singtel, which is also listed on its own.

merchants.name: Singtel
merchants.notes: Singtel mobile and broadband bills. The GXS Credit Card pays 1.75% on Singtel bills with no minimum spend; Singtel Shop purchases (devices and accessories) are a yuu merchant on the DBS yuu card but count as shopping, not bills. Assumed to be about a third of telco bills (Singtel is the largest operator).
